The assistant cannot change bed states. ## Emergency and priorities The emergency snapshot records counts awaiting assessment, awaiting a bed and staff-assessed high/medium/low priority counts. No patient-level records or automated triage model are connected. The assistant must not infer patient priority or recommend treatment. Operational task priorities routine/urgent are not patient triage categories. ## Forecast model and input history Demand forecast requires 13–120 consecutive completed months: month, total_ae_attendances, emergency_admissions, attendances_under_4_hours, decision_to_admit_waits_over_4_hours. Current/future input months are rejected. Staff submit these through the Demand forecast screen or its CSV importer. New submissions now save the validated input history with their forecast. Legacy forecast records do not contain their original input history; submit the history again before asking the assistant to rerun the model. Partial shift records do not replace the monthly staff-hour budget. Equipment stocks are context and are not optimiser constraints. Staff must mark unusable beds appropriately. Tasks are staff-owned follow-up records. Recommendations await administrator approval; approval records a decision but does not execute bed/staff allocation. The assistant has no approval or record-editing tools. ## Assistant and document evidence The assistant combines Groq generation, locally computed BGE-small embeddings, stored policy passages, semantic/keyword retrieval, and hospital-scoped backend tools. Only retrieved excerpts and selected record summaries are sent to Groq. Documents are shared across this installation. An uploaded document is not automatically an approved hospital policy. Answers should cite the actual retrieved passage IDs and hospital/tool evidence. When evidence is absent, say what is missing. Free-tier quotas may delay or prevent generation; no successful action should be claimed after a failed tool.
